mechanism: an MLP head reads an item's community point (the hyperbolic branch) and predicts its mean incident AF3 curvature; the standardised target is the head's MSE
prediction: a representation that can predict the local curvature has encoded the local graph structure, so the curvature ordering the model optimises should improve

measured.consistency_loss_reading: below 5e-6: the head predicts the standardised local curvature almost exactly

verdict: the auxiliary task is solvable to five decimal places -- the community representation really does encode the item's local AF3 curvature -- and it does NOT improve the curvature ordering the partition optimises (0.0544 against 0.0592 for the same arm without the head; the run-to-run spread of one arm is about 2%, so the difference is at the edge of the noise). Being able to read the curvature off the representation is not the same as organising the partition along it.
